The [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]] language had its own accompanying '''writing system''' of the same name.<ref name="Ziro Concept">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/hunt-for-ziro-concept-art-gallery|text="Hunt for Ziro" Concept Art Gallery}} {{C|Slide 3}}</ref> 

==History==
Huttese inscriptions could be seen on the walls of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] at the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]].<ref name="TOR" /> 

During the [[Boonta Eve Classic (32 BBY)/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] on the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]-controlled [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] where young [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] won his freedom, Huttese numbers were used on the lap counter in the [[Mos Espa Grand Arena/Legends|Mos Espa Grand Arena]], featuring the numerals for "3", "2" and "1". The console monitors on [[Anakin Skywalker's Podracer/Legends|his podracer]], and [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|Shmi Skywalker's]] viewscreen, also featured Huttese numerals.<ref name="TPM" />

Advertisements for [[Converter Station/Legends|Converter Station]] and [[Hutt's Grotto/Legends|Hutt's Grotto]] at [[Stobar Spaceport/Legends|Stobar Spaceport]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] were written in this alphabet.<ref name="Brothers" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:NalHuttese-123.png|thumb|left|The first three Huttese digits]]
The Huttese alphabet was created for the [[1999]] movie [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], in which it was featured during the [[Podracing/Legends|podracing]] sequence. Huttese inscriptions were notably shown on Anakin Skywalker's Podracer control panels. The numerals for "3", "2" and "1" were also featured on the lap indicators at the Mos Espa Grand Arena.<ref name="TPM" /> The same numerals appeared in the 1999 video game [[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Racer'']].<ref name="SWE1R">[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Racer'']]</ref>

The same glyphs were used in the [[Nar Kreeta]] level of the [[2003]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]'', although occurrences of that alphabet were written in mirror image when compared to ''The Phantom Menace''.<ref name="JK:JA" /> Those inscriptions were written according to the mapping of a fanmade "Nal-Huttese" font that could be found at Geocities.com as early as [[July]], 1999.<ref name="Geo">{{WebCite|url=http://geocities.com/TimesSquare/4965/sffont.html#huttese|text=''Star Wars'' Nal-Huttese font|date=2009-10-04|work=[[Wikipedia:GeoCities|GeoCities]]|archivedate=20091021030053|nolive=1}}</ref> The readable Huttese inscriptions in the game are "BALE," "RANCOR," "OPEN," "CLOSED," and "PARLOR," all of which made sense in context.<ref name="JK:JA" />

[[File:NalHuttese.png|thumb|Nal Huttese graffiti.]]
While the original Nal-Huttese font only contained letters A-S, an updated version emerged later on EagleFonts.com, a searchable database of free TrueType fonts.<ref name="Eagle">{{WebCite|url=https://www.eaglefonts.com/nal-huttese-ttf-97906.htm|text=Nal-Huttese|work=[https://eaglefonts.com eaglefonts.com]|archivedate=20200507082848|nolive=1}}</ref> That new version was included in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''. Inscriptions on planet Coruscant are consistent with spelling the phrases "Black Sun" and "The sun shall rise." On the [[Vaiken Spacedock]], a board hanging above the doorway leading to the Hutta departures clearly reads "Hutta."<ref name="TOR" />

Despite the aforementioned evidences to the contrary, [[Leland Chee]], who maintains the [[Holocron continuity database]], has stated that the updated Geocities font has not been officially endorsed. When asked about that by a Wookieepedia editor on his Facebook account, Chee stated: "Though [the updated Geocities font] has many similarities to a font we have based on letters and numbers seen in The Phantom Menace, this is not an official font. No official fonts have ever been made publicly available."<ref name="FBChee">{{Facebook|noprofile=1|author=[[Leland Chee]]|date=2013-05-10|quote=No official fonts have ever been made publicly available.|url=permalink.php?story_fbid=136364006552017&id=201820953172172&comment_id=133605&offset=0&total_comments=2|nolive=1|nobackup=1}}</ref>

In concept art for the [[Pongeeta-class swamp speeder|Hutt swamp speeder]] created for the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' episode "[[Hunt for Ziro]]," there is a warning in Huttese around the [[Engine/Legends|engines]], reading "DANGER STATIC ELECTRICITY".<ref name="Ziro Concept" /> However, this detail does not appear in the final episode.<ref name="Ziro">{{TCW|Hunt for Ziro}}</ref>

A [[Painting/Legends|poster]] created by [[Will Nichols]] for the [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] of the [[Turtle Tanker/Legends|Turtle Tanker]] in the ''The Clone Wars'' episode "[[Brothers (episode)|Brothers]]," depicts a [[Color/Legends|purple]]-skinned [[Togruta/Legends|Togruta]] accompanied by the letters "''[[Sop|SOP]]''" in Huttese.<ref name="Nichols BlogSpot">{{Blogspot|subdomain=willnicholsportfolio|url=2018/04/vehicles.html|name=WILL NICHOLS PORTFOLIO|text=VEHICLES|date=2018-04-02}}</ref><ref name="NicholsArtStation">{{ArtStation|subdomain=songjong|username=songjong|name=[[Will Nichols|William Nichols]]|url=projects/w9OyZ|text=Star Wars Clone Wars Revenge 4x22 ship|date=2016-10-03|quote=This was a ship (space truck) I designed for Clone Wars. It was stolen and piloted by Savage and Maul. Ventress and Kenobi would team up to fight them in the ship. There were a lot of little details in the ship (posters, twi'lek hula girl) that I designed that didnt make it into the ship but would be used later in other episodes.}}</ref> However, the poster does not appear in the final episode.<ref name="Brothers" />
